Business data map

Entities, relationships, state machines, automatic processes, integrations and the flows that move data in Bunkai TMS. Built from the app repo at origin/staging (de0ee80, migrations 0001 to 0096), migration 0097 on branch feature/BK-593-run-step-evidence, and the live database read through the DB MCP.

Overview

Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System. The data model has one ownership spine and one traceability chain:

  • Ownership spine. Workspace, then Project, then Module (a tree), then User story, then Acceptance criterion. Every row resolves its tenant by walking back to workspace_id, and row-level security on every table is keyed on the caller's active membership in that workspace.
  • Traceability chain. Acceptance criterion, then ATC (anchored to at least one criterion), then Test (an ordered chain of ATC references), then Run (a frozen snapshot of that chain executed against a project environment), then Bug (filed from a failed run step, or standalone). Test Plans group Tests, and reports read the whole chain.

Business rules live mostly in Postgres. Writes go through bunkai_* RPCs (SECURITY DEFINER or INVOKER) that validate, lock rows, write the change and append an activity_log row in one transaction. Triggers on activity_log fan events out to notifications. Two pg_cron jobs and one Vercel Cron run the scheduled work.

Actors: human members with a workspace role (viewer, member, admin, owner), AI agents and CI pipelines through Personal Access Tokens (a Run records executor_mode = human, agent or ci), the service role (background workers, cron, webhooks) and two QA inspection database roles.

Entities

The live database holds 41 tables in schema public, all with row-level security enabled. Row counts are the planner's estimates (pg_class.reltuples) on 2026-10-19, read through the DB MCP: they show which tables carry real test data, not exact numbers.

Key relationships

  • A project's foreign keys cascade to its modules, stories, criteria, ATCs, environments, Runs, Bugs, Milestones and Test Plans. But test_steps.atc_id is RESTRICT and Tests belong to the workspace, so a project whose ATCs are chained in any Test should fail to delete; no project delete path was looked for, so this is the schema's behaviour, not a verified product flow.
  • A user story cannot be deleted while an ATC points at it (atcs.user_story_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT). An ATC cannot be deleted while a Test chains it (test_steps.atc_id RESTRICT). A Test cannot be deleted while a Run references it, and an environment cannot be deleted while a Run used it (both RESTRICT on runs).
  • Snapshots survive their source: run_atcs.atc_id, run_steps.atc_step_id and the Bug provenance columns (run_id, run_step_id, atc_id) are SET NULL, so evidence outlives an edited or removed ATC.
  • Tests belong to a workspace, not a project, so one Test's chain may include ATCs from several projects of the same workspace.

Workspace: plan and soft deletion

A workspace carries a plan (community, cloud, enterprise) and, since 0084, soft-delete columns (deleted_at, deletion_requested_by). Once deleted_at is set, every membership helper treats the workspace as gone: access ends at once for every member, including the owner, during a 30-day grace period. Migration 0089 extended the same guard to the explicit-actor helpers used by headless (PAT) routes, after an ex-member was found to keep access to Tests, Runs and ATCs during the grace window (BK-991).

The plan limits live as TypeScript constants in lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts, and the database mirrors only the project limit, in a trigger:

PlanSeatsProjectsRetention window (days)Enforced where
community5330Projects: trigger bunkai_enforce_project_limit. Seats and retention: displayed only
cloud255090Same
enterpriseunlimitedunlimitedunlimitedSame

Seats count active members only (invited and suspended members never count). The retention figure is shown as usage; nothing in the product prunes Runs (0072 header).

Module: tree, path and archive

Modules form a self-referential tree (parent_module_id) with a materialized slash-separated path, unique per project and limited to 6 levels by a CHECK. A move re-bases the path of the module and every descendant in one function. Archiving sets archived_at on the module subtree and its stories and ATCs (soft delete); reports and lists filter archived rows out, while a single Bug filed against an archived module stays readable and is tagged "Archived" (0070). Every structural change writes an activity_log row (0023).

ATC: anchoring, version and classification

  • Anchoring. An ATC belongs to one project, one module and one user story, and must link to at least one acceptance criterion of that story through atc_acceptance_criteria.
  • Edits. Create and update go through bunkai_create_atc / bunkai_update_atc; an update replaces the steps and assertions wholesale (step ids are not stable across edits) and increments version. Because Tests hold references, an edit reaches every Test that chains the ATC at once (0035 reports the affected Test ids); Runs already started keep their snapshot.
  • Duplicate. bunkai_duplicate_atc deep-copies steps, assertions and criterion links into a new ATC in the same project, with a fresh slug and version 1.
  • Classification. layer is required (UI, API, Unit). Since 0087, technique (Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis, State Transition, Decision Table, Pairwise) and priority (Critical, High, Medium, Low) are optional; older rows stay NULL.
  • Guards. A title minimum length (0058) and a cap on tags (0065) are enforced in the database. tsv is a full-text vector over title and tags, rebuilt by a trigger.
  • atcs.status is a dead column. It accepts unrun, running, pass, fail, blocked, skipped, but execution results live in run_atcs; migration 0050 calls atcs.status "the dead column" and moved coverage to read run history instead.

Test: a chain of references

A Test (capital T) is a workspace-scoped container holding an ordered chain of ATC references in test_steps. It never copies ATC content: the copy happens when a Run starts. The chain can be reordered (the multiset of ATCs must stay identical, guarded by a version column) and tagged with the reserved suite tags smoke, sanity, regression plus free-text tags.

Because Tests have no project_id, a Test's project is derived through its chain. Adding a Test to a Test Plan requires the whole chain to resolve inside the plan's project: an empty chain or a chain that touches another project is refused with one uniform error (0076).

Run snapshot

Starting a Run (bunkai_create_run) walks the Test's chain and freezes one run_atcs row per chain position and one run_steps row per executable step, all pending. The Run also snapshots its module (0040), records executor_mode and executor_user_id, and points at a project_environments row. Since 0092, a trigger stores source_atc_id on every run_atcs row so two Runs of the same Test can be compared step by step even after the ATC was edited.

The verdict of a run ATC is recomputed from its steps whenever a step is marked. Results never flow back into atcs.

Bug: provenance and sync state

A Bug always belongs to a workspace, a project and a module. When filed from a failed run step it also keeps run_id, run_step_id and atc_id as provenance; a standalone Bug has all three NULL and the detail page reads that as "Filed manually". A trigger (bunkai_bugs_check_consistency) rejects any row whose project is outside its workspace, whose module is outside its project, whose run is outside its project, whose run step is outside its run or whose ATC is outside its project.

Columns added by 0091 prepare the Jira sync: sync_state is one of not_applicable, pending, syncing, synced, failed. Saving a project's tracker settings re-queues that project's stranded Bugs. No application code that sends a Bug to Jira was found on origin/staging (see Discovery gaps).

Test plan

A Test Plan is a project-level container with a name (unique per project, case-insensitive, internal whitespace collapsed; NBSP is preserved since 0074) and a goal. It has no delete: Close is the only exit from Open. Writes happen only through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs; the tables have no client write policy. Any member with write access may edit any plan; created_by is for display, except that closing is allowed to the creator (with write access) or an admin or owner.

Progress is computed, never stored while open: each member Test counts with the outcome of its latest Run, whenever that Run happened (passed, failed, aborted, in_progress, not_run), and passed% = floor(passed / members × 100). Closing freezes that progress into progress_snapshot together with the verdict and summary.

Secret tables and the QA database roles

Three sibling tables hold only SHA-256 hashes: access_token_secrets, workspace_invite_secrets and magic_link_token_secrets. Postgres cannot hide one column, so the hashes were moved out of the main tables (0011, 0012) and the QA roles are denied these three tables. The planner still exposes their row estimates, which is why the live catalog lists 41 tables while information_schema shows 38 to the QA role.

The QA roles qa_inspector_ro and qa_inspector_rw bypass RLS and hold table CRUD (read-only for _ro). Since 0085 and 0086 they can also execute the business RPCs, except five SECURITY DEFINER functions that read auth.users. Most RPCs bind the actor to auth.uid(), which is NULL on a direct database session, so calling them from the DB MCP usually fails closed. The _ro role is explicitly kept away from write-capable DEFINER functions (0088). The schemas cron and supabase_migrations are not readable by the QA role.

Flow: first workspace

  1. A signed-in user with no active membership is sent to onboarding.
  2. POST /api/v1/workspaces validates the slug (format, reserved words, uniqueness).
  3. bunkai_bootstrap_workspace inserts the workspace (plan community) and the caller's owner membership in one SECURITY DEFINER transaction, which solves the chicken-and-egg of "you must be a member to insert a member".

Rule: the creator is always the owner. Rule: a new workspace is on the free plan, so its fourth project is refused by the project-limit trigger.

Flow: sign-in and token issuance (data side)

The request shapes and the login state machine belong to infra-context (section architecture, Auth flow). The data effects:

  • auth_email_status (0034) answers whether an email exists and is confirmed, because the auth schema is not exposed to the API.
  • Headless sign-in and signup confirmation mint a PAT: one access_tokens row (12-character indexed token_prefix, scopes, optional workspace binding and expiry) and one access_token_secrets row with the hash. The raw token is returned once.
  • Every Bearer call looks up the prefix, compares the hash, rejects revoked or expired tokens with a uniform 401, and updates last_used_at without blocking.
  • workspace:admin is never a default scope and is refused at sign-in. Migration 0033 revoked the tokens that had been issued with it illegitimately (BK-135).

Flow: invite a teammate

  1. An admin or owner posts an email and a role (viewer, member or admin: owner cannot be invited, a CHECK enforces it). An email that already belongs to an active member is refused (0022).
  2. The invite row gets expires_at = now + 7 days; the token hash goes to workspace_invite_secrets. The API returns the accept link once. No email is sent: the inviter shares the link.
  3. The invitee, signed in with the same email, posts the token to /api/v1/invites/accept. Revoked, already accepted and expired invites each answer 409 with their own message; an invite into a deleted workspace answers as revoked.
  4. On success the membership is upserted as active with the invite's role and accepted_at is stamped, so the invite is single-use.

Flow: from story to ATC

  1. A member creates a user story in a module. Its Jira key (external_id) is unique per project (0016), which is what makes a repeated import safe.
  2. Criteria are added and reordered; ordering ignores archived criteria and is atomic (0017).
  3. The story moves to ready_to_test only through bunkai_set_user_story_status, which locks the story and requires at least one active criterion (error 45010 ac_required_for_ready_to_test). Archiving a criterion takes the same lock, so a story cannot end up ready with zero criteria.
  4. An ATC is created through POST /api/v1/atcs (cookie or PAT) with steps, assertions and criterion links; the RPC writes all of it plus an activity_log row in one transaction.

Flow: Jira import

  1. POST /api/v1/imports enqueues a queued job. A partial unique index allows only one queued or running job per project; a second request answers 409 import_in_progress.
  2. A worker in Vercel's after() slot claims the job with the service-role client, moves it to running, pages through Jira's JQL search and upserts user stories and criteria (Markdown sanitized on the way in).
  3. Per-issue failures accumulate in errors; bad credentials fail the whole job. The job ends completed or failed. The UI polls its status.

Flow: execute a Run

  1. Start. bunkai_create_run checks write access, validates executor_mode (45200), requires an environment configured for the Test's project (45201) and at least one executable step (45202), then freezes the snapshot.
  2. Mark. bunkai_mark_run_step sets one step to passed, failed or blocked (never back to pending, 45213), stamps executed_at, and recomputes the run ATC's verdict. It locks the Run row, so marks, finish and abort serialize. A closed Run refuses marks (45212). Changes replicate through Supabase Realtime for live views (0043).
  3. Finish. bunkai_finish_run sets the verdict (passed or failed, 45207 otherwise) and finished_at; pending steps become skipped. Only a running Run can finish (45206): the first terminal call wins.
  4. Abort. bunkai_abort_run requires a reason of 3 to 500 characters (a CHECK enforces it) and also skips pending steps.
  5. Audit and notify. Finish and abort write run.finished / run.aborted into activity_log with via = cookie or bearer (0067), which the notification trigger uses to decide whether to notify the person who started the Run.

Rule: the same write gate applies to a human, an AI agent and CI; executor_mode records who executed, it grants nothing.

Flow: file and triage a Bug

  1. A member files a Bug from a failed run step (provenance kept) or standalone, with title, severity P1 to P4, project and module. The consistency trigger rejects mismatched provenance.
  2. Triage: bunkai_assign_bug assigns, reassigns or unassigns an owner who must be an eligible workspace member; bunkai_transition_bug_status moves the status forward one step at a time. Both read auth.uid() and are called through the caller's RLS client, so they work for a browser session and for a PAT (whose calls carry a short-lived user JWT), never for the service role.
  3. Each change writes bug.assigned, bug.reassigned, bug.unassigned or bug.status_changed to activity_log, which feeds notifications.

Non-disclosure: a missing Bug and a Bug in a workspace the caller does not belong to both answer bug_not_found; only a member without write role sees forbidden.

Flow: notifications and the daily digest

  1. An RPC appends an event to activity_log.
  2. Two AFTER INSERT triggers on activity_log pick the events that notify: bunkai_notify_bug_event (bug assigned, reassigned, unassigned, status changed) and bunkai_notify_run_event (run finished, run aborted). They insert one notifications row per recipient, with a snapshot so the entry still renders after the entity is deleted. The triggers do not read notification_preferences (verified in the live function bodies).
  3. The inbox shows a recipient's rows for 90 days while they remain a member (RLS policy).
  4. Every day at 08:00 UTC, Vercel Cron calls POST /api/v1/admin/send-digest with a CRON_SECRET bearer. The route inserts a pending row per (user, day) in notification_digest_log before sending (a second concurrent run conflicts and skips), emails unread notifications through Resend, then marks the row sent or failed.

Preferences are negative state only: no row means on. The only place they are applied is the digest candidate query, which drops a notification when the user has an explicit enabled = false row for channel email and that event group. The in_app preference is stored but no code that applies it was found.

Only five event types ever produce rows: run.finished, run.aborted, bug.assigned, bug.reassigned, bug.status_changed. bug.unassigned passes the trigger filter but always computes zero recipients (0078 header). A run event is not sent to its own starter when they ended it interactively (via = cookie).

Flow: plan, track and close a Test Plan

  1. Create or edit a plan (name, goal). A duplicate name in the project fails on the unique index (23505, answered 409).
  2. Add or remove Tests: each Test must resolve entirely inside the plan's project; a pair already present fails on the unique index, behind the Idempotency-Key middleware. Edits and membership changes on a closed plan answer 45603 test_plan_not_open.
  3. Progress is read live from the members' latest Runs.
  4. Close (bunkai_close_test_plan): verdict passed or failed is required (45604, 45605), summary optional up to 4000 characters after trimming; the plan row is locked, the progress snapshot is stored, and test_plan.closed is logged. A caller who is neither the creator with write access nor an admin or owner gets 45606.
  5. Reopen (bunkai_reopen_test_plan) clears verdict, summary and snapshot and logs test_plan.reopened; the history stays in activity_log.

Flow: reports read the chain

Reports have no tables of their own; each is one RPC over the live chain.

ReportRPCBusiness rule
Project coveragebunkai_report_project_coverageAn ATC counts as executed only when its most recent run ATC is passed or failed; skipped, blocked, pending and no run all read "not run" (0090 fixed the earlier count, which hit 130 of 152 ACs with run history on staging). A failed ATC still covers its criterion.
Story traceabilitybunkai_report_story_traceabilityOne story's criterion → ATC → Test → Run → Bug chain in one call, with the module of each ATC; the project is derived from the story's module, never from the nullable user_stories.project_id.
Recovery cyclebunkai_report_project_recovery_cyclesPer story, time from the first failing Run to the first later all-passing Run; run data only, no Bug data.
Defect heatmapbunkai_report_project_defect_heatmapBugs per module with a week-over-week trend for a 7, 30 or 90 day window (default 30).
Project Runs0041 report RPCA project's Runs filtered, with pass and fail totals.
Run comparebunkai_compare_runA Run against the previous finished Run of the same Test and environment, pairing steps by ATC occurrence and exact step text.
Workspace search0071 search RPCOne full-text search across ATCs, Tests, Projects, Modules, Bugs and Runs, filtered by each table's own RLS.

Every report answers a missing, foreign or non-member target with the same not-found result, so a report never confirms that another workspace's object exists.

Flow: upgrade to the paid plan

  1. An admin or owner sees plan, active seats, project count and oldest-run age (bunkai_workspace_billing_overview-style RPC from 0072; a non-admin gets 404).
  2. Upgrade inserts a billing_checkout_sessions row (target plan always cloud) BEFORE calling Stripe, and passes that row's id as client_reference_id. A partial unique index allows one open session per workspace, so two tabs cannot open two checkouts.
  3. The user pays on Stripe's hosted Checkout.
  4. Stripe calls /api/v1/billing/webhook. The handled events are checkout.session.completed, .async_payment_succeeded, .async_payment_failed and .expired; any other type answers 200 ignored. bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event finds the session row, flips the workspace plan to cloud only when Stripe's payment_status is paid, stores the Stripe customer and subscription ids, and records the event id in stripe_webhook_events so a redelivery is applied once. Failed and expired sessions release the one-open-session lock.

Flow: export workspace data

  1. The owner, from a browser session only (never a PAT), requests an export: a queued row in workspace_exports, at most one in flight per workspace. A trigger logs the request in activity_log.
  2. A Vercel after() worker with the service-role client collects the workspace data, builds the archive and stores it in a private Supabase Storage bucket; the row ends completed (with expires_at = completion + 168 hours) or failed.
  3. Each download re-checks owner, ready and not expired through bunkai_resolve_workspace_export_download, which also writes export.downloaded. There is no signed URL. Errors: 45801 no export yet, 45802 not ready, 45803 expired.

Flow: delete and restore a workspace

  1. The owner calls bunkai_request_workspace_deletion. Non-owners get 45900; a workspace already deleted gets 45901 (double-submit guard).
  2. The function sets deleted_at, writes a workspace_deletions tombstone with purge_deadline = now + 30 days, the member count and a row-count digest, and returns the members' emails; the app then emails them (no email leaves Postgres).
  3. Access ends immediately for everyone. Members cannot veto.
  4. During the grace period the owner can call bunkai_restore_workspace_deletion, which only clears deleted_at (no data moves). Restoring a live workspace answers 45902.
  5. The pg_cron job bunkai-purge-deleted-workspaces runs daily at 03:00 and purges workspaces past their deadline; the cascade removes the workspace data, and the tombstone stays with purged_at.

Flow: attach screenshot evidence to a run step (in flight)

Defined by migration 0097 on branch feature/BK-593-run-step-evidence, not merged to staging, but its tables and trigger already exist in the live database (the team applies migrations to the shared database before merging).

  1. Init: the RPC checks the Run is running and the caller may write, then creates a pending attachment row with an upload deadline and returns a Storage signed upload URL.
  2. The browser uploads the file directly to the private bucket (bytes never pass through a Vercel function).
  3. Commit: the row becomes committed and visible to every workspace member.
  4. Limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP, 10 MiB per file, 10 files and 50 MiB per step, 250 MiB per Run. A terminal Run is read-only forever; only the uploader may remove their own attachment while the Run is running.
  5. Deleting a row fires run_step_attachments_enqueue_cleanup, which queues the Storage object in storage_cleanup_queue; a daily sweep route drains the queue and expires stale pending rows.

Errors: 45216 Run not running, 45217 limit exceeded (hint names which), 45218 pending upload expired, 45219 not the uploader.

Integration: Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime, Storage)

  • Postgres 17 holds all product data and most business rules. Down means the product is down.
  • Auth issues sessions, sends signup OTPs and magic links, brokers GitHub and Google OAuth. PAT callers are turned into a short-lived user JWT so RLS applies to them too (details in infra-context).
  • Realtime replicates run and step changes for live run views (0043).
  • Storage holds workspace export archives (private bucket, service role only) and, with BK-593, run step screenshots (private bucket, signed upload URLs).

Integration: Jira Cloud

  • Inbound: the import job pulls issues into user stories and criteria. Throttling (429) retries with backoff; bad credentials fail the job. Flows depending on it: Jira import.
  • Outbound (configured, not shipped): project_tracker_settings and the Bug sync columns exist; credentials are deployment-level only, never stored per project. No sender was found.

Integration: Stripe

Data out: a Checkout Session per upgrade attempt. Data in: checkout webhooks that flip the plan to cloud. If Stripe is down, upgrades cannot start; if webhooks are delayed, the plan changes late and the session stays open (blocking a second checkout) until a webhook or expiry arrives. Subscription renewal, cancellation and downgrade events are not handled.

Integration: email (Resend and Supabase Auth mail)

  • Supabase Auth sends signup OTPs and magic links (through custom SMTP per the app's /qa page).
  • The app sends the daily digest and the workspace-deletion notices through Resend.
  • Invites still send no email: the inviter shares the link.

If email fails, signup and magic-link login stop for new users, the digest row ends failed, and deletion notices may not reach members (deletion itself still happens).

Integration: Vercel

Hosts the app and runs its background work: the after() slot for the Jira import and workspace export workers, and Vercel Cron for the digest. A long import or export must finish within the function's time limit; there is no queue to resume it.

Discovery gaps

  • Local app clone is stale. ../upex-bunkai-tms sits 537 commits behind origin/staging (local c0712e9, 2026-08-06). This map was built from origin/staging after a git fetch, without changing the working tree. The domain map and the infra map were generated from the stale clone and still state 31 tables and 67 migrations.
  • Unmerged schema in the shared database. run_step_attachments, storage_cleanup_queue and their trigger come from migration 0097 on feature/BK-593-run-step-evidence. Staging's database may run ahead of staging's code.
  • Migrations 0079 and 0080 are absent from origin/staging; I could not verify whether they were renumbered, abandoned or applied from another branch. The QA role cannot read supabase_migrations to check the ledger.
  • Cron jobs were read from migration source, not from the live cron.job table (permission denied for the QA role). Whether they are active on this database is not verified.
  • Which environment the DB MCP points at: assumed staging (testing.default_env); row estimates come from that connection.
  • Member suspension: the suspended status exists but no code path that sets or clears it was found.
  • Story back to draft: the CHECK allows ready_to_test → draft; the business conditions were not verified.
  • Bug sync to Jira: configuration and sync-state columns exist, but no sender was found on origin/staging (only tests and generated types reference sync_state).
  • Stripe lifecycle beyond checkout: no handling of renewal, cancellation, failed renewal or downgrade was found; a workspace that stops paying keeps cloud as far as this code shows.
  • Seat and retention limits are displayed but not enforced; I found no gate that blocks the sixth member on community.
  • Milestone lifecycle: no status column; whether a milestone can be completed or archived is unknown.
  • Feature flag rows: the planner has no estimate for feature_flags, and no API reads it.
  • Storage cleanup sweep schedule (BK-593) not verified.
  • Exact function names of the project-runs report (0041), the workspace search (0071) and the billing overview (0072) were not read; the table names them by migration.
